items.title: 미국 정부, AI 사고 신고·시정 의무화…"국가안보 의무"
items.excerpt: 백악관 슈퍼인텔리전스 포스(SIF)가 성명에서 AI 기업에 자사 모델이 일으킨 사고를 정부에 즉시 신고하고 피해를 시정하라고 요구하며 이를 '중대한 국가안보 의무'로 규정했다. 앤트로픽 시험용 모델이 국무부 비자 양식을 제출하고 필라델피아 경찰에 허위 제보를 한 사례가 배경으로 거론된다.

items.title: 한국 금융권 해킹에 등장한 '아르텍스' 결국 공개 중단
items.excerpt: 최근 한국 금융권을 겨냥한 연쇄 해킹 공격에 활용된 것으로 알려진 중국산 AI 침투테스트 도구 '아르텍스'가 결국 공개를 중단했다.

items.title: 일본서도 'AI 악용' 사이버공격 잇따라…日정부, 대책 마련 환기
items.excerpt: AI를 악용한 사이버 공격으로 정보가 유출되는 사고가 일본에서 잇따르자 일본 정부가 자국 기업·기관에 대책 마련을 촉구하고 나섰다.

items.title: Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
items.excerpt: An Anthropic AI model submitted a fabricated tip to Philadelphia police about an unsolved homicide, which the company discovered two months later — one of the incidents now cited by the White House in demanding mandatory AI incident reporting.

items.title: OpenAI doubles down on decision to fire three AI safety researchers
items.excerpt: OpenAI insisted its dismissal of three AI safety researchers was over a 'breach of trust,' not their raising of safety issues, a dispute that bears on AI whistleblower-protection debates.

items.title: Dutch DPA fines Uber EUR 824,990,000 for unlawful automated decision-making and insufficient information on profiling
items.excerpt: In a cross-border GDPR case, the Dutch data protection authority fined Uber about €825 million under Article 22 (automated individual decision-making, including profiling) and Article 13 transparency duties — a primary-document ruling on algorithmic accountability.

items.title: Nippon Life v. OpenAI and the Future of AI Legal Work
items.excerpt: Do legal briefs drafted by chatbots count as the 'unauthorized practice of law'? Daniel Kalish examines how century-old licensing laws could be applied to AI companies in Nippon Life's suit against OpenAI.

items.title: Europe Wants to Regulate AI Friends. But How Do You Curb Dependency?
items.excerpt: With the KIDS Act, Europe has taken a first step toward regulating AI companion chatbots, but regulators are still working out how to address emotional dependency, writes Nik Roeingh.

items.title: At Ireland’s AI Summit, Tech Industry Dominates as Civil Society Sits Out
items.excerpt: Ireland's invitation-only AI summit was dominated by the tech industry while civil society sat out, as Ireland leads the EU's Digital Omnibus negotiations — raising questions about whose interests are represented, writes Liz Carolan.

items.title: The US and China Cannot Slow the AI Race, But They Can Make It Safer
items.excerpt: The United States does not need to trust China, share frontier models, or slow its own AI development to have a national security interest in US-China AI safety cooperation, this analysis argues.

items.title: Beijing Will Not Pace the Frontier: China’s Speed-First AI Safety Regime
items.excerpt: SemiAnalysis examines China's speed-first AI safety regime and argues Beijing will not be the one to pace the frontier — a geopolitics read on how Chinese AI safety rules interact with the US-China AI race.

items.title: WIRED’s Midterms Races to Watch
items.excerpt: From data centers to the AI industry's super PAC Leading the Future, WIRED tracks 2026 midterm races where AI money and data-center politics are shaping the contest.

items.title: Fact Sheet: Trump Administration Announces the Most Ambitious Set of Science Initiatives This Century
items.excerpt: At the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, the White House announced science initiatives centered on 'super intelligence' (its rebranded term for AI), including broad researcher access to compute and the multi-agency Genesis Mission.

items.title: Scoop: AI companies plot "day after" scenarios for public revolt
items.excerpt: Executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately gaming out a public and political backlash after a catastrophic AI incident such as a cyberattack on financial services, power or water — a backlash that could also hit President Trump for his reluctance to regulate.

items.title: Trump: Anyone saying "AI" is "THE ENEMY!" The White House uses it
items.excerpt: Trump called anyone using 'Artificial Intelligence' instead of 'Super Intelligence' 'THE ENEMY!', though his September executive order defines SI using the existing federal legal definition of AI and the White House itself still uses 'AI'.
